scope: Source and assay provenance, not independent experimental evidence. Original machine source objects and selected caches are preserved. Raw tool responses and full literal record inventories remain in the review work packet.

source_counts.note: Raw GOA and original seeded YAML remain exact; projection duplicates retain provider/date distinctions in raw evidence.

PMID:12134079.access_scope: Exact main abstract preserved. Selected Methods and Results were read from the separately archived genuine normal full PMC117323 variant; no current-product alignment is inferred from historical numbering.
PMID:12134079.finding: Human CLN5 constructs interact with CLN2/TPP1 and CLN3 in cell-free and cellular assays. Antibody and translation-start differences separate lysosomal signals from ER/Golgi precursor signals; the 2002 TPP1 binding assay uses precursor material.

PMID:14699076.access_scope: Exact main abstract preserved. Selected Methods and Results were read from the separately archived genuine normal full PMC363135 variant.
PMID:14699076.finding: CLN3 targeting-motif mutants retain association with CLN5 in COS-1 coexpression assays; this interaction is distinguished from a requirement for CLN3 lysosomal targeting.

PMID:22431521.access_scope: Exact main abstract preserved. Authentic original PMC3347407 full HTML was recovered externally; selected Methods and Results were read with paragraph hashes.
PMID:22431521.finding: CLN5 associates with sortilin, Rab5 and Rab7 in cells. Depletion impairs Rab7 loading, retromer recruitment and receptor recycling, with a rescue comparison; no purified GEF activity or membrane-spanning scaffold mechanism is established.

PMID:32296183.access_scope: Selected genuine normal full Results, Discussion and assay/validation legends were read. The selected cache has no separate Methods section; no separate Methods or figure-pixel inspection is claimed.
PMID:32296183.finding: Exact positive binary-screen records support six CLN5 partners, with tagged and fragment-specific scopes preserved. Systematic retesting and sequence verification strengthen the interaction dataset without assigning physiological context to every pair.

PMID:16399764.access_scope: Complete abstract and authentic publisher-indexed target Table I and assay text read; direct publisher/MCP downloads failed, and the Elsevier response contained metadata only. This is not a complete original full-text read.
PMID:16399764.finding: CLN5 is positively identified in MPR-affinity-purified material as a mannose-6-phosphorylated glycoprotein. This is glycan-carriage evidence; the receptor is the recognition reagent, so the assay does not substantiate CLN5 lectin activity.
PMID:16399764.target_table: Table I, CLN5: human log(e) −34 and mouse log(e) −24; positive MPR-affinity capture, not a CLN5 lectin assay.

PMID:20052765.access_scope: Exact authentic abstract preserved; original full journal text was not recovered. The author thesis, printed pages 64–67, describes study-I experiments but does not reproduce the journal article in the recovered PDF. Later PMID:26342652 full text supplies independent processing evidence.
PMID:20052765.finding: The original abstract reports maturation and lysosomal targeting of CLN5 itself. The author thesis describes precursor cleavage, glycosylation and trafficking experiments; the source does not establish CLN5 as the enzyme or cofactor performing protein maturation.

PMID:24038957.access_scope: Complete authentic selected abstract read; original full text was not recovered. No original figure-pixel or detailed Methods claim.
PMID:24038957.finding: The authentic abstract distinguishes type-II precursor topology, signal-peptide cleavage and mature luminal membrane association through an amphipathic region. Mutant ER retention is separate from normal lysosomal localization.

PMID:24058541.access_scope: Selected actual full-text Methods, Results and Discussion paragraphs read from the authenticated normal source. No figure-pixel or whole-paper claim.
PMID:24058541.finding: Human CLN5 glycosylation mutants distinguish folding, trafficking and stability effects. Wild-type protein localizes with LAMP2 and within enlarged Rab5 endosomes; covalent glycans are not a mannose-binding assay.

PMID:28442266.access_scope: Complete authentic selected abstract read; original full text was not recovered. No original figure-pixel or detailed Methods claim.
PMID:28442266.finding: The original abstract describes SPPL3 cleavage of a historical 407-residue CLN5 precursor into a soluble lysosomal fragment. CLN5 is the substrate of this cleavage, not the protease.

PMID:11971870.access_scope: Complete authentic selected abstract read; original full text was not recovered. No original figure-pixel or detailed Methods claim.
PMID:11971870.finding: The authentic abstract reports lysosomal colocalization, glycosylation and secretion of expressed human CLN5 in BHK-21 cells, supporting a soluble lysosomal protein.

PMID:19941651.access_scope: Selected actual full-text Methods, Results and Discussion paragraphs read from the authenticated normal source. No figure-pixel or whole-paper claim.
PMID:19941651.finding: The paper separates mouse CLN5 fusion-protein binding experiments from human CLN5 localization in HeLa and SH-SY5Y cells. Wild-type and trafficking-defective constructs differ; PPT1 overexpression can rescue mutant CLN5 trafficking without proving the converse.

PMID:37708259.access_scope: Complete authentic selected abstract read; original full text was not recovered. No original figure-pixel or detailed Methods claim.
PMID:37708259.finding: The authentic abstract reports CLN5-mediated BMP formation and cellular LPG/BMP changes. Independent later purified-enzyme work supports a bounded BMP-forming capacity but does not assign S,S-BMP stereoinversion to CLN5.

PMID:11722572.access_scope: Original publisher full-text Methods, Table 1, Results and Discussion were recovered and read at https://febs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1046/j.0014-2956.2001.02530.x. The protected publication cache remains abstract-only; external full access is recorded separately. No original figure pixels were inspected.
PMID:11722572.finding: Patient-cell lysosomal pH is elevated in the tested CLN5 line; the recovered original Discussion leaves direct and indirect mechanisms unresolved.

PMID:10992246.access_scope: Complete authentic selected abstract read; original full text was not recovered. No original figure-pixel or detailed Methods claim.
PMID:10992246.finding: The authentic abstract describes CLN5 expression in developing human brain and postmitotic migrating neuroblasts. The original subcellular images and additional developmental evidence remain inaccessible.

PMID:35427157.access_scope: Selected actual Methods, Results, Figure 5 legend and Discussion were reread from the authenticated full cache. The positive NPC-lysate result and the authors’ artificial-substrate caution are both retained. No figure-pixel or whole-paper claim. Original supplementary substrate details remain inaccessible.
PMID:35427157.finding: Purified CLN5 and deficient-NPC lysate assays support thioesterase capacity; Figure 5 motivates the authors’ neuronal interpretation, while the Discussion cautions that artificial substrates leave physiological substrate specificity unresolved. The Results/legend differ in NPC species labeling. No CoA-specific assay was verified.

PMID:9662406.access_scope: Complete authentic selected abstract read; original full text was not recovered. No original figure-pixel or detailed Methods claim.
PMID:9662406.finding: The original cloning report identifies disease-associated CLN5 and predicts membrane features. Later processing and localization studies qualify the precursor-versus-mature-protein interpretation.

PMID:10740217.access_scope: Complete authentic selected abstract read; original full text was not recovered. No original figure-pixel or detailed Methods claim.
PMID:10740217.finding: This early NCL review presents CLN3 and CLN5 functions as unknown and proposes a shared catabolic context. It does not directly demonstrate a CLN5-performed protein-breakdown reaction.

PMID:23533145.access_scope: Actual main Methods and Results read from the exact main cache. Original Table S2 was identified but returned 403; the CLN5 target entry remains uninspected. Main-text availability does not mean the supplement was read.
PMID:23533145.finding: The actual main Methods describe extracellular-vesicle enrichment from expressed prostatic secretions in urine. The inaccessible supplementary protein table prevents independent verification of the CLN5 target entry.

PMID:29128403.access_scope: Complete authentic selected abstract read; original full text was not recovered. No original figure-pixel or detailed Methods claim.
PMID:29128403.finding: The authentic abstract reports glycoside-hydrolase activity for both Dictyostelium and human CLN5. Exact substrates, purification and specificity controls remain unverified because original full text was not recovered.

PMID:39423811.access_scope: Selected actual full-text Methods, Results and Discussion paragraphs read from the authenticated normal source. No figure-pixel or whole-paper claim.
PMID:39423811.finding: The published study directly measures purified CLN5 making R,racemic BMP but not S,S-BMP; PLD3/4 perform the stereoinversion-associated pathway. Its unchanged BMP phenotype after CLN5 deletion is cell-context specific.

PMID:39548099.access_scope: Selected actual full-text Methods, Results and Discussion paragraphs read from the authenticated normal source. No figure-pixel or whole-paper claim.
PMID:39548099.finding: CLN5-deficient HEK293 cells retain basal BMP in standard serum but lose most BMP after extended culture with heat-inactivated serum. The study experimentally demonstrates extracellular lipid supply as a modifier of the phenotype.

PMID:41890119.access_scope: Selected actual full-text Methods, Results and Discussion paragraphs read from the authenticated normal source. No figure-pixel or whole-paper claim. Explicit preprint status retained; lysate assays are not described as stereochemically resolved purified-enzyme reactions.
PMID:41890119.finding: This 2026 preprint reports reduced labeled-LPG-to-BMP conversion in CLN5-deficient lysosomal lysates and rescue by recombinant human CLN5. It is not peer reviewed and does not resolve product stereochemistry in an isolated-enzyme assay.

PMID:26342652.access_scope: Selected actual full-text Methods, Results and Discussion paragraphs read from the authenticated normal source. No figure-pixel or whole-paper claim.
PMID:26342652.finding: Human-cell pulse-chase, endogenous-antibody controls and protease inhibitors establish CLN5 C-terminal processing in acidic compartments. CLN5 is the processed substrate; the responsible cysteine protease remains unidentified.

PMID:15459177.access_scope: Complete authentic selected abstract read; original full text was not recovered. No original figure-pixel or detailed Methods claim.
PMID:15459177.finding: The authentic mouse knockout abstract reports lysosomal storage material and progressive neural pathology, providing experimental grounding for the curated lysosome-organization premise.

PMID:15207259.access_scope: Complete authentic selected abstract read; original full text was not recovered. No original figure-pixel or detailed Methods claim.
PMID:15207259.finding: The authentic abstract identifies mouse Cln5 expression and describes soluble lysosomal localization in expression systems, corroborating the exact experimental lumen donor record.

ontology_terms.label: membrane
ontology_terms.definition: A lipid bilayer along with all the proteins and protein complexes embedded in it and attached to it.

ontology_terms.label: D-mannose binding
ontology_terms.definition: Binding to mannose, a monosaccharide hexose, stereoisomeric with glucose, that occurs naturally only in polymerized forms called mannans.

ontology_terms.label: neuron maturation
ontology_terms.definition: A developmental process, independent of morphogenetic (shape) change, that is required for a neuron to attain its fully functional state.

ontology_terms.label: retrograde transport, endosome to Golgi
ontology_terms.definition: The directed movement of membrane-bounded vesicles from endosomes back to the trans-Golgi network where they are recycled for further rounds of transport.

ontology_terms.label: protein catabolic process
ontology_terms.definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of a protein by the destruction of the native, active configuration, with or without the hydrolysis of peptide bonds.

ontology_terms.label: lysosomal membrane
ontology_terms.definition: The lipid bilayer surrounding the lysosome and separating its contents from the cell cytoplasm.

ontology_terms.label: lysosome
ontology_terms.definition: A small lytic vacuole that has cell cycle-independent morphology found in most animal cells and that contains a variety of hydrolases, most of which have their maximal activities in the pH range 5-6. The contained enzymes display latency if properly isolated. About 40 different lysosomal hydrolases are known and lysosomes have a great variety of morphologies and functions.

ontology_terms.label: Golgi apparatus
ontology_terms.definition: A membrane-bound cytoplasmic organelle of the endomembrane system that further processes the core oligosaccharides (e.g. N-glycans) added to proteins in the endoplasmic reticulum and packages them into membrane-bound vesicles. The Golgi apparatus operates at the intersection of the secretory, lysosomal, and endocytic pathways.

ontology_terms.label: vacuolar lumen
ontology_terms.definition: The volume enclosed within the vacuolar membrane.

ontology_terms.label: endoplasmic reticulum
ontology_terms.definition: The irregular network of unit membranes, visible only by electron microscopy, that occurs in the cytoplasm of many eukaryotic cells. The membranes form a complex meshwork of tubular channels, which are often expanded into slitlike cavities called cisternae. The ER takes two forms, rough (or granular), with ribosomes adhering to the outer surface, and smooth (with no ribosomes attached).

ontology_terms.label: cytosol
ontology_terms.definition: The part of the cytoplasm that does not contain organelles but which does contain other particulate matter, such as protein complexes.

ontology_terms.label: protein binding
ontology_terms.definition: Binding to a protein.

ontology_terms.label: protein maturation
ontology_terms.definition: Any process leading to the attainment of the full functional capacity of a protein.

ontology_terms.label: hydrolase activity, acting on glycosyl bonds
ontology_terms.definition: Catalysis of the hydrolysis of any glycosyl bond.

ontology_terms.label: obsolete macromolecule depalmitoylation
ontology_terms.definition: OBSOLETE. The removal of palymitoyl groups from a macromolecule.

ontology_terms.label: extracellular exosome
ontology_terms.definition: A vesicle that is released into the extracellular region by fusion of the limiting endosomal membrane of a multivesicular body with the plasma membrane. Extracellular exosomes, also simply called exosomes, have a diameter of about 40-100 nm.

ontology_terms.label: palmitoyl-(protein) hydrolase activity
ontology_terms.definition: Catalysis of the reaction: palmitoyl-protein + H2O = palmitate + protein.

ontology_terms.label: long-chain fatty acyl-CoA hydrolase activity
ontology_terms.definition: Catalysis of the reaction: a long-chain fatty acyl-CoA + H2O = a long-chain fatty acid + CoA + H+. A long-chain fatty acid has an aliphatic tail containing 13 to 22 carbons.

ontology_terms.label: positive regulation of GTP binding
ontology_terms.definition: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of GTP binding.

ontology_terms.label: perinuclear region of cytoplasm
ontology_terms.definition: Cytoplasm situated near, or occurring around, the nucleus.

ontology_terms.label: neurogenesis
ontology_terms.definition: Generation of cells within the nervous system.

ontology_terms.label: bis(monoacylglycero)phosphate synthase activity
ontology_terms.definition: Catalysis of the reaction: 2 3-acyl-sn-glycero-1-phospho-(1'-sn-glycerol) = 3-acyl-sn-glycero-1-phospho-(3'-acyl-1'-sn-glycerol) + sn-glycero-1-phospho-(1'-sn-glycerol).

ontology_terms.label: lysosome organization
ontology_terms.definition: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of a lysosome. A lysosome is a cytoplasmic, membrane-bounded organelle that is found in most animal cells and that contains a variety of hydrolases.

ontology_terms.label: lysosomal lumen acidification
ontology_terms.definition: Any process that reduces the pH of the lysosomal lumen, corresponding to an increase in hydrogen ion concentration.

ontology_terms.label: brain development
ontology_terms.definition: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the brain over time, from its formation to the mature structure. Brain development begins with patterning events in the neural tube and ends with the mature structure that is the center of thought and emotion. The brain is responsible for the coordination and control of bodily activities and the interpretation of information from the senses (sight, hearing, smell, etc.).

ontology_terms.label: protease binding
ontology_terms.definition: Binding to a protease or a peptidase.

ontology_terms.label: endoplasmic reticulum lumen
ontology_terms.definition: The volume enclosed by the membranes of the endoplasmic reticulum.

ontology_terms.label: lysosomal lumen
ontology_terms.definition: The volume enclosed within the lysosomal membrane.

ontology_terms.label: phosphatase binding
ontology_terms.definition: Binding to a phosphatase.

ontology_terms.label: small GTPase binding
ontology_terms.definition: Binding to a small monomeric GTPase.

ontology_terms.label: insulin-like growth factor binding
ontology_terms.definition: Binding to an insulin-like growth factor, any member of a group of polypeptides that are structurally homologous to insulin and share many of its biological activities, but are immunologically distinct from it.

ontology_terms.label: insulin-like growth factor I binding
ontology_terms.definition: Binding to insulin-like growth factor I.

ontology_terms.label: insulin-like growth factor II binding
ontology_terms.definition: Binding to insulin-like growth factor II.
